newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST -Guinness to show dull growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -Guinness to show dull growth.

text.p: Drinks group Guinness Plc is set to report only a very modest 1996 profits increase on Thursday, held back by a dull performance from its spirits arm, United Distillers.
Analysts forecast a 2.5 percent increase in pre-tax profits, with most expectations centred around 960-965 million stg, up from 940 million last time.
"There should be some evidence that the outlook is slowly improving with respect to both volume and price increases on spirits," said Merrill Lynch analyst Mark Puleikis.
"For the first time in a number of years we are starting to see some small volume improvement and modest inflation." he added.
Merrill's forecast pre-tax profits of 965 million stg at the top end of the range 945 to 968 million. A total dividend of 16 pence per share is anticipated, up from 14.9 pence.
Guinness brewing should show a seven percent improvement in trading profits to 289 million while the spirits business, United Distillers, is forecast to report flat profits of 677 million stg.
In January the company said sales by UD were one percent higher than in 1995 with notable growth in single malts and de luxe Scotch whiskies.

It added that UD achieved price rises of three percent or more during 1996 in the United States, Britain, Latin America, Eastern Europe and the Middle East. The effect of these price increases will be around 1.5 percent for 1996, it said.
At Cruzcampo, the company's troubled Spanish brewer, Guinness said profits are expected to be broadly in line with 1995 due to improved productivity.
The company warned that the strong pound would cut profits by six percent or 60 million stg in 1997 compared to 1996 assuming current exchange rates hold.
Many analysts are also hoping for a buy-back of 100 million shares or a special dividend of up to 25p, possibly as early as results day itself.
Guinness announced a buy-back of shares worth 460 million stg, representing five percent of the company, the day after its 1995 results.
Analysts will also want to see the company increase its marketing spending by a minimum 10 percent on its 500 million stg level in 1995.
Guinness shares were up 3p at 476p on Friday, against a high of 498p for the year.
